title_en: GTA 6 User Reviews on Metacritic Show Its Getting Review Bombed by People Who Haven't Played the Game, But Why?
summary_en: Why GTA 6 user reviews are so low: Metacritic review-bombing explained.
body_en:
GTA 6 tied with the original version of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time as the highest-scored game in history based on Metacritic ratings, sitting pretty at a 99 critic score. Rarely do we see something earn this kind of unanimous praise, but our reviewer Luke Reilly would agree , giving GTA 6 a coveted score of 10 on our scale and calling it “the single most impressive video game I have ever played." However, you may have heard about the wide discrepancy between the critic's metascore and the user score — as of publishing this, GTA 6 has a 5.7/10 average from well over 100,000 user reviews. Why is that?
User scores on Metacritic are under far, far (and I mean far ) less scrutiny, allowing everyone and anyone to post their own review and score regardless of how much of the game they've actually played. This isn't anything new, and it’s been around on other sites that aggregate scores from the audience (like Rotten Tomatoes or an older version of GameSpot I used to use as a kid). As a result, you're likely to see more outliers or trolling, but mostly users who shoot from the hip to let their voice be heard. That leaves things susceptible to review bombing – typically, a wave of reactionary people who have motives beyond evaluating a game for what it is.
There are reviews that appear to have legitimate concerns, mentioning that GTA 6 might not be for them or align with their tastes. Among those concerns are a slow start that emphasizes slice-of-life style activities before action starts to pick up, dissatisfaction with the interactive layers for simple tasks, the frame rate being capped at 30 fps, or a general disinterest in what it's trying to do as an open-world action game. Maybe it didn't live up to their perceived "hype" with 13 years between series entries. However, you might be wondering why GTA 6 is the latest subject of what's clearly motivated review bombing with tons of "0" scores from a reactionary crowd.
I'm not going to pretend to give credence to clearly disingenuous reviews, but if you are genuinely curious, there are a significant number of reviews that decry GTA 6 for being "too woke" and a, uh, "cuck simulator” — the most unserious people, the incel crowd coming out of the woodwork, trying to fight a weird culture war over a game they likely either did not play or have barely played. GTA has always parodied the most ridiculous parts of American culture, and GTA 6 is no exception — now the primary targets of that satire are crying about it.
I don't think I need to explain what it means to be a "cuck" or the concept of cuckoldry, but by definition, it has nothing to do with anything that happens to you or that you have to do in GTA 6. And perhaps the most telling part of it all is the complaints of "woke" (another term that has been ground to a point of no meaning, co-opted by right-wing extremists to label anything they deem politically progressive).
In large part, GTA 6 is telling a love story where two partners, the protagonists Jason and Lucia, have a believable relationship on-screen with corresponding gameplay elements in addition to their Bonnie and Clyde-esque crime sprees. Maybe you don't want to put up drywall, renovate your house, or run errands in early missions, but what you're about to read is more telling about the kind of people review-bombing the game than the content of the game itself.
Sift through the negative reviews on Metacritic and it's a trove of entries that read, "Everything that represents the woke culture don’t deserve nothing, other than zero." Or, "GTA 6 is way too woke for my taste." And other variations on one that reads, "Graphics fantastic, besides that a cuckhold [sic] game, and really woke!" One just spams the word "woke" while several are straight gibberish or admittance that they did not play the game.
One entry reads, "I already have an annoying gf in real life and you want me to deal with it in the game again???????", while another says, "No hookers, no freedom, No action, Just cuck simulator, Please woke community, leave Rockstar games alone." And (sorry) one more for the road: "The plot is boring, and the main characters are a simp and a stereotypical ‘strong woman.’ They have absolutely no charisma; the game is packed with a one-sided agenda, and the trolling of ‘libturds’ is dull and predictable."
Amid this all, Metacritic has some measures in place to moderate fake reviews — it removed user reviews that went live before the game even released . And its 36-hour rule has been in place for a while where user reviews can't go up until a day-and-a-half has passed from a game's public release. Moderators also have the ability to stamp out reviews that violate Metacritic's guidelines, but with well over 100,000 of them up now, it's a gargantuan task.
While that crowd continues to be petty, whatever dent they think they're making isn't visible, as publisher Take-Two Interactive reported $3.79 billion in revenue with approximately 32.5 million units sold by launch day. Rockstar is going to be fine. Like the game or not, outrage fatigue is settling in; this perceived culture war is as meaningless as it's ever been, and it's best to pay it no mind to save yourself from the psychic damage.
